title: Deterministic toolchain and layer profiling to cut CI flakiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our CI variance and occasional nondeterministic build failures increase iteration time and obscure real test regressions. Root causes include floating toolchain versions in base images, non-reproducible npm/pip installs, and inconsistent Docker layer ordering across builders. Goal: reduce CI flakiness by introducing deterministic, version-pinned toolchain manifests, a reproducible build image pipe, and a CI layer-profiling step that surfaces expensive/unstable layers so we can prioritize caching and refactors.

Scope:
- Define and publish a deterministic toolchain manifest for build images (gcc/clang, node, python, bazel/pip versions).
- Introduce a staged image build pipeline that enforces layer ordering and produces a signed image manifest per commit.
- Add a lightweight layer-profiling job that runs on main for changed Dockerfiles and reports top-5 slowest layers and cache miss rates.
- Convert top 3 flaky build jobs to use the pinned manifests and test reproducibility across remote builders and local dev.

Constraints & non-goals:
- We will not replace the entire build fleet in this ticket; this is incremental.
- Runtime production images and release artifacts are out of scope (we focus on builder images and CI-facing reproducibility).
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic toolchain manifest (YAML) exists in infra/toolchains/ with explicit versions and checksum references for primary toolchains.
CI pipeline step `ci/toolchain-validate` fails if a builder image deviates from the manifest
Layer profiling job posts a short report to the PR with top-5 slow layers and cache miss percentages (run on main for changed Dockerfiles).
Three previously flaky CI jobs demonstrate consistent rebuild times across two successive runs (variance < 10%).
Documentation updated in Confluence with migration steps for devs and a rollback plan.
notes: We prioritise developer ergonomics: manifests should be easy to bump via a single PR and validated by CI. Signed manifests allow traceability for incident postmortems.
risks: Initial manifest bumps may require several follow-up PRs to get transitive deps stable.
Remote builder heterogeneity could still cause rare mismatches; add telemetry to detect drift.
Long-running dependency updates may temporarily increase image sizes if not optimized.
next_steps: Finalize toolchain manifest schema and add to infra repo (owner: Luca).
Implement `ci/toolchain-validate` step and add to PR and main pipelines (owner: CI eng).
Prototype layer-profiling job using existing buildkit logs and upload small report to PRs (owner: Aisha).
